market_holds: Spot $8.33 at the 2026-11-10 seal (baseline). The stock is +57% since the close before the Q2 print ($5.27 on 2026-08-11, Yahoo bars) and +31% since the Q2 reaction close ($6.32). The bigger leg came 22-24 Sep, when it went from $6.35 to $7.91 on 5-7m shares a day; no company news was found for those days, and Truist raised its target to $9 on 09-28. The high was about $9.15-9.23 in late October and the stock has since slipped about 9% into the print (20d -1.5%, 5d -3.4%). Consensus Q3 revenue is about $103.9m (+26.9%) and non-GAAP EPS $0.04, whisper $0.05 (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-03). That consensus is simply management's own number: on the Q2 call (2026-08-12) the CFO said 'We expect third quarter revenue growth of approximately 27%' and Q3 gross-profit growth 'similar to' Q2's 13%. FY26 guide: revenue $400-410m and adj. EBITDA $33-39m. With H1 at $187.0m and Q3 at about $104m, the guide implies Q4 at about $114m, only +15% on Q4 2025's $99.3m (own arithmetic). The CFO also said take rates will run 'slightly lower' and the GMV-to-revenue spread will narrow. Average sell-side target is about $6-6.5 and mostly Hold, below spot, so the price has gone past the analysts. Short interest is about 1-1.7% of float, so no crowded short. Front-expiry ATM IV is 131.8% against 50.5% realised, which points to a large event move, but the ATM spread is 145% of mid and too wide to read. Call-heavy open interest (put/call 0.17) and skew that pays for upside. Past bmo reactions at the close: Aug-26 +19.9%, May-26 +4.6%, Mar-26 -6.2%, Nov-25 +1.4%, Mar-25 +3.0%, Aug-24 -22.8%. Typical size about 5-15%.
view: The trigger for the Q2 re-rating was a stale Street ($89.2m consensus against $98.7m reported) plus a guidance raise. That gap is gone. Consensus now sits on management's explicit 27% Q3 guide, so the print turns on two things: whether Q3 beats the company's own number, and whether the Q4-implied +15% gets raised. The freshest outside data leans to upside on both. Digital Finance, i.e. event contracts and gaming, was the growth engine (+~180% y/y in Q2, ACH volume ~19x). Kalshi's Q3 cash volume was $37.3bn, +76% q/q, with a record September. Total prediction-market volume hit a record ~$123bn in October against ~$75.5bn in September, so Q4 has started hot. That is the kind of datapoint the payments analysts covering RSKD may not model. Three things temper it. Management set the 27% guide on 08-12 already knowing July, and Kalshi's July and August cash volume ($12.3bn, $11.4bn) was flat-to-down, so most of the quarter was inside their visibility and only September adds clear upside. Riskified does not disclose its Digital Finance share or its merchants, so the read-through could be small. And margins are the known worry: GP growth guided at only 13% against 27% revenue growth, with the take rate compressing. After a 57% run the stock needs a beat and a raise, though the slide off the October high lowers that bar a little. A small beat plus a modest FY raise is my central case. That favours up, but not by enough, and not on evidence direct enough to clear 65%.
unpriced: Possibly the size of the Q4 guide raise. The FY guide implies Q4 growth of about +15% after a guided +27% Q3, while prediction-market volume, the category's driver, set a fresh record in October. Sell-side models anchored on that guide may not track prediction-market data. Riskified's exposure to it is undisclosed, though, so I cannot show the gap is large.

recommendation.reason: The release should show a beat of the 27% guide and a FY raise, helped by Kalshi's Q3 cash volume (+76% q/q) and record October prediction-market volume feeding Digital Finance. But consensus already equals management's guide, management had July in hand when it set the guide, the category's revenue share is not disclosed, and the stock has run 57% since the last print with margin compression a known worry. The edge is a lean, not a 65% call.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A FY revenue guide raised clearly above ~$415m with Q3 GP growth above 13% would make the up case decisive. Q3 revenue at or below ~$104m, or GP margin falling below ~45% with no Q4 raise, would make it a down print after the run.

self_critique: The up case rests on one public series (prediction-market volume) whose link to Riskified's revenue is undisclosed and could be small. Volume is inflated by cheap parlays and is not card or ACH deposits, which is what Riskified actually screens. Management guided with July in view, and the CFO flagged take-rate compression. After a 57% run with targets below spot, an in-line quarter plus a guide nudge could still sell off, as in Mar-26 (-6.2%). Hawkish macro (hot CPI, December hike odds) also weighs on small-cap momentum names in a window that ends at 13:00 ET.
approach_notes: The 'priced in is a claim to prove' step paid off: finding the explicit 27% Q3 guide showed the consensus is management's number, which killed the stale-estimate thesis. The freshest-data-first step led to the prediction-market series, which helped but could not be tied quantitatively to the company's revenue.
